title: fix(llm): keep verified OpenRouter models discoverable
body:
<!-- Keep this PR as draft until it is ready for review. -->

<!-- AI/LLM agents:
Do not edit the HUMAN section.
-->

HUMAN:
This PR fixes a bunch of regressions that happened on main, because LiteLLM removed OpenRouter from its model catalog .json file, and OpenHands relies on that.

To note, there was no LiteLLM upgrade, but LiteLLM serves this .json over HTTP… so when it changed in main, it broke. 😢 

https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/45669

<!--
Human author: please replace this comment with a short note (at least 20 visible
characters) before marking ready for review.
AI agents: you must not edit this section.
-->

---

AGENT:

## Why

LiteLLM 1.93.0 loads its model catalog from upstream main at import time. [The upstream OpenRouter catalog removal](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/45669) made `/api/llm/models?provider=openrouter` return an empty list and broke the OpenRouter router and SDK catalog tests on unchanged main. The failure also appears in [PR 5700](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/pull/5700).

## Summary

- Include curated, verified OpenRouter routes in SDK model discovery with their `openrouter/` prefix, independently of LiteLLM's cost map.
- Exercise the HTTP filter with fixed catalogs both containing and omitting OpenRouter entries; preserve catalog-only routes, sorting, deduplication, and provider isolation.
- Replace live-catalog model and capability assertions with SDK contract checks, correct curation guidance, and move an MCP test Action to module scope so it cannot invalidate later event deserialization.

## Issue Number

Fixes #5704. Reproduced on main while investigating [PR 5700](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/pull/5700).

## How to Test

`uv run pytest tests/sdk/llm/test_model_list.py tests/sdk/llm/test_model_features.py tests/sdk/llm/test_runtime_metadata.py tests/sdk/tool/test_mcp_schema.py tests/sdk/tool/test_response_schema.py tests/sdk/tool/test_tool.py tests/agent_server/test_llm_router.py -q` — 347 passed.

Per-file pre-commit checks passed for all seven changed files.

CI on final commit `282fc9984c9be7cef3ad87d723267b873782016c`: [the full test workflow](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/actions/runs/38095608510) passed, including 6970 SDK tests, the Agent Server suite, and cross-package tests. [Linux, macOS, and Windows binary builds and smoke tests](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/actions/runs/38095608471), TypeScript integration, pre-commit, REST API compatibility, and persisted-settings compatibility also passed.

Before/after evidence on macOS with Python 3.13.11, LiteLLM 1.93.0, and its actual remote catalog (no local-catalog override or patched model data):

- Base `c4b93299c`: HTTP `GET /api/llm/models?provider=openrouter` returned 200 with `{"models": []}`. Both original catalog-dependent tests failed. The new deterministic SDK regression also failed before the implementation change.
- Fixed checkout: the same request returned 200 with 21 correctly prefixed routes, including `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-chat`.
- On both revisions the existing OpenRouter endpoints adapter resolved that route to a 128000-token runtime context limit. Model discovery adds no network requests.

The first CI run exposed three additional capability assertions tied to the removed OpenRouter catalog and four schema-deserialization failures caused by a locally defined test Action retained in subclass caches. All seven were reproduced together locally before the test corrections and pass afterward. The capability checks now verify SDK forwarding of LiteLLM support, including proxy-prefix normalization; production capability policy is unchanged.

The HTTP check used the real FastAPI application through TestClient; the catalog and OpenRouter metadata requests used live upstream services. CI runs on Linux.

## Video/Screenshots

HTTP before/after results are included above; no visual UI changes.

## Design Doc

The focused discovery change and regression coverage are described above.

## Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Docs / chore

## Notes

Corresponding documentation: https://github.com/OpenHands/docs/pull/924

Response schemas and provider filtering are unchanged. The curated routes remain discoverable; additional OpenRouter models still come from LiteLLM's catalog. Context limits continue to use the existing OpenRouter runtime metadata adapter.

HUMAN:

This PR is a follow-up to #5661 that closes the remaining deferred-initialization gaps by applying the shared readiness gate consistently across protected HTTP and Canvas backend ingress.

---

AGENT:

## Why

Protected ingress must wait until deferred initialization has published the
runtime configuration before evaluating credentials. Canvas backend ingress is

- Add deterministic transition-race coverage plus a real Uvicorn/wsproto
  lifecycle regression.

## Issue Number

Related to #5688.

## How to Test

title: fix(agent-server): reject blank and redacted secret values
body:
HUMAN:

This PR fixes the silent secret deletion reported in #5623. The API now rejects unusable values without modifying existing data, preventing an apparently successful secret edit from erasing the stored credential and breaking downstream workflows.

---

AGENT:

## Why

`PUT /api/settings/secrets` accepts empty, whitespace-only, and redacted-placeholder values. Persistence normalizes these values to `null`, which can erase an existing secret or create a listed secret that cannot be read.

## Summary

- Reject blank and redacted-placeholder values with HTTP 422 before persistence.
- Leave existing secret values and descriptions unchanged when an invalid upsert is rejected.
- Cover new-secret and existing-secret behavior through router and live-server tests.

## Issue Number

Fixes #5623

## How to Test

```bash
uv run pytest tests/agent_server/test_settings_router.py tests/cross/test_remote_conversation_live_server.py::test_settings_and_secrets_api_with_live_server -q
uv run pre-commit run --files openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/settings_router.py tests/agent_server/test_settings_router.py tests/cross/test_remote_conversation_live_server.py
```

Result: 85 tests passed, and pre-commit passed.

## Video/Screenshots

title: feat(workspace): add SmolMachinesWorkspace to run the agent server in a microVM
body:
<!-- Keep this PR as draft until it is ready for review. -->

<!-- AI/LLM agents:
Do not edit the HUMAN section.
-->

HUMAN:

<!--
Human author: please replace this comment with a short note (at least 20 visible
characters) before marking ready for review.
AI agents: you must not edit this section.
-->

---

AGENT:

## Why

Adds a workspace that runs the agent server inside a smol machine, a hardware-isolated microVM with its own kernel, for users who want VM isolation and egress control without a Docker daemon.

## Summary

- `SmolMachinesWorkspace` in `openhands.workspace.smolmachines`, a `RemoteWorkspace` like `ApptainerWorkspace`, behind a new `smolmachines` extra (Linux with KVM, Apple Silicon macOS).
- Supports `mount_dir`, `allow_hosts` / `allow_cidrs` egress limits, host env forwarding, and `keep_alive` reuse of a named machine after checking its host-owned port and forwarded environment; policy changes select a new VM, and a host-state directory inside the mounted project is rejected.
- Uses the agent server's V1 session key when forwarded, falling back to the legacy key only when it is the one sent to the VM; unit tests with a fake SDK and an example excluded from the examples run.

## Issue Number

None.

## How to Test

Unit: `uv run --frozen pytest -q tests/workspace/test_smolmachines_workspace.py` (15 pass, including session-key precedence and cleanup retries); Ruff and Pyright pass on changed files, and `uv run --frozen pytest -q tests/workspace` passes all 223 tests (two existing Docker-workspace teardown warnings).

Earlier end-to-end run on Linux x86_64 with KVM and `smolmachines` 1.22.1, with the default agent driven by a scripted OpenAI-compatible model:
- a conversation's terminal call ran inside the machine (guest kernel 6.12.95, host's `~/.ssh` not visible) and wrote into the mounted project as the host user;
- with `allow_cidrs` set to only the model's address, the agent loop completed and the terminal could not reach example.com;
- with `keep_alive`, a second workspace reused the same machine and disk.

With `smolmachines` 1.25.2 on Linux x86_64/KVM, a real `ghcr.io/openhands/agent-server:latest-python` VM passed HTTP `/health` and `workspace.execute_command("printf OH_VM_OK")` returned exit 0 and `OH_VM_OK`; a stopped `keep_alive=True` machine restarted on its recorded port and still had `/workspace/marker.txt`, then was deleted. On both local and Cloud VMs, `allow_hosts=["example.com"]` allowed that host and refused unlisted `www.python.org`.

On the current head with `smolmachines` 1.22.2, a real local microVM ran the agent server with distinct `OH_SESSION_API_KEYS_0` and `SESSION_API_KEY` values; the workspace authenticated using the V1 key, executed `printf OPENHANDS_AUTH_OK`, and deleted the VM on exit.

## Video/Screenshots

N/A.

## Type

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Docs / chore

## Notes

The lockfile diff contains only the new optional dependency and its wheel metadata; the agent server, health check, workspace command, and stopped-machine reuse were validated against a real local VM.

title: test(integration): make token condensation deterministic
body:
HUMAN:

I have confirmed the code here and it looks good.

---

AGENT:

## Why
The original c04 asks for 1,000 individual echo calls. GPT-5.5 declined that workload before reaching the 5,000-token threshold, producing a false failure. Preserve its real terminal-tool loop and condensation coverage while generating sufficient output in two bounded calls.

## Summary
- Replace the 1,000-call instruction with two separate Python terminal commands, each printing 2,000 repetitions of a short phrase.
- Raise the token threshold to 6,000 and keep the seeded context small so a single tool result clears it by a wide margin on every CI model.
- Set `keep_first=2` so the user instruction survives the first condensation and the second command still runs.
- Raise the iteration cap from 10 to 20 so the two condensations, the summarizer calls they trigger, and the tool turns all fit within budget.
- Require at least two condensations in `verify_result`, so the second cycle is actually enforced rather than merely observed.
- Remove the obsolete long-loop refusal skip.

## Issue Number
Closes #5674

## How to Test
Live evaluations of the revised test (not the earlier oversized-user-message implementation):

```bash
LLM_BASE_URL=https://llm-proxy.app.all-hands.dev LLM_API_KEY=... \
  uv run python tests/integration/run_infer.py \
  --llm-config '{"model":"litellm_proxy/openai/gpt-5.5","reasoning_effort":"high"}' \
  --test-type condenser --eval-ids c04_token_condenser
LLM_BASE_URL=https://llm-proxy.app.all-hands.dev LLM_API_KEY=... \
  uv run python tests/integration/run_infer.py \
  --llm-config '{"model":"litellm_proxy/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6","temperature":0.0}' \
  --test-type condenser --eval-ids c04_token_condenser
uv run pre-commit run --files tests/integration/tests/c04_token_condenser.py
```

- Both CI condenser models (GPT-5.5 and Sonnet 4.6) pass repeatedly, each reporting two condensations with the first summarizing four events.
- Each run executes the two commands separately, with an LLM summary between them, and reaches the second-condensation pause.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks pass, including Ruff, pycodestyle, Pyright, import rules, and registration checks.

Review feedback from VascoSch92 addressed; all review threads resolved.

body:
HUMAN: adding DigitalOcean as a verifid provider. --- AGENT: ## Why DigitalOcean Inference should be selectable as an LLM provider (pick "DigitalOcean", pick a model, paste a DO key). Today it only works through Advanced settings (`openai/` + a custom base URL), and LiteLLM's native `gradient_ai/` route can't be used for agents because it rejects `tools`. ## Summary - `litellm_call_kwargs` now resolves routed SDK prefixes from one small table: `openhands/` → `litellm_proxy/` + the OpenHands proxy (unchanged), and `digitalocean/` → `openai/` + `https://inference.do-ai.run/v1`. A user-provided `base_url` still wins. - `VERIFIED_MODELS["digitalocean"]` adds a short curated list of DO model IDs (taken from `GET /v1/models`), so DigitalOcean appears in the verified section of the provider/model pickers. Only Chat Completions models with tool calling; the gpt-6 line is left out because DO needs the Responses API for its tools. ## Issue Number Closes #5666 ## How to Test Unit tests: ``` uv run pytest tests/sdk/llm tests/cross tests/agent_server/test_llm_router.py ``` `tests/sdk/llm` + `tests/cross`: 1734 passed, 1 skipped; router tests pass; pre-commit (ruff, pycodestyle, pyright, import rules) is green on the changed files. Live check against DigitalOcean (one tool-calling request per model, using exactly the kwargs `litellm_call_kwargs("digitalocean/", None)` produces, with a DO token as `api_key`): ``` PASS glm-5.3: tool_calls=['get_weather'] PASS anthropic-claude-sonnet-5.5: tool_calls=['get_weather'] PASS openai-gpt-5.6-luna: tool_calls=['get_weather'] ``` ## Video/Screenshots N/A (no UI change in this repo). ## Type - [ ] Bug fix - [x] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Breaking change - [ ] Docs / chore ## Notes - LiteLLM has no metadata for these models, so context window / max tokens fall back to defaults; registering them is a possible follow-up. - Follow-ups outside this repo: Agent Canvas display name (`digitalocean: "DigitalOcean"` in `src/utils/map-provider.ts`) and SDK pin bump in OpenHands/OpenHands; a short docs entry in OpenHands/docs. ---

title: test(integration): validate hard reset semantics in c02
body:
HUMAN: This seems to have fixed the test. --- AGENT: ## Why The v1.54.0 release evaluation reports `c02_hard_context_reset` failing across every evaluated model because it still treats `summary_offset == 0` as the hard-reset contract. Since #5242, hard reset intentionally preserves the leading `SystemPromptEvent` and places the generated user-role summary after it so subsequent LLM requests remain system-first. The runtime behavior is correct; the stale evaluation expectation and model-dependent setup are not. ## Summary - make c02's hard-reset trigger deterministic without relying on model-generated event counts - validate the actual reset semantics: preserve the system prompt, forget all other prior history, insert the summary after it, and produce a system-first LLM request - verify continued execution and a later normal condensation that preserves the hard-reset summary; align the integration README ### REST API contract changes Compared with base OpenAPI `330441825052` for public `/api/**` paths. ```diff --- base public OpenAPI +++ head public OpenAPI @@ -1581 +1581 @@ -schema Event oneOf=[ServerErrorEvent,ACPToolCallEvent,Condensation,CondensationRequest,CondensationSummaryEvent,ConversationErrorEvent,ConversationStateUpdateEvent,HookExecutionEvent,LLMCompletionLogEvent,ActionEvent,MessageEvent,AgentErrorEvent,ObservationEvent,UserRejectObservation,SystemPromptEvent,StreamingDeltaEvent,TokenEvent,InterruptEvent,PauseEvent]
